docs.title: Zeta Global Hands-on Lab & Hackathon
docs.text: Welcome to the Cloudera AI Hands-on Lab and Hackathon guide for Zeta Global technical teams. This documentation is your reference for the entire event — from logging into the Cloudera platform through building and deploying your hackathon project.

docs.title: Guide Contents
docs.text:
This guide walks you through:

  1. Login & Workbench Setup — Access the Cloudera Data Platform and connect to the shared AI workbench.
  2. Project Creation & Runtimes — Create your team project and configure Python runtimes.
  3. Vibe Coding with Cloudera AI — Use Cursor (Remote SSH) or Claude CLI with private model inference for AI-assisted development.
  4. Sample Code: Data Upload — Load sample metric data into your project using the provided notebook and JSON file.
  5. Demo Videos & Interactive Tours — Watch the custom data loading demo and explore guided tours of Cloudera AI.

docs.text: Resource Link Login URL CDP Workshop Login GitHub Repository SuperEllipse/zeta-hol Sample Data (JSON) sample_metric_data.json Data Load Notebook dataload_notebook.ipynb

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
Before you begin, ensure you have received the following from your instructor:

  • Username and password for the Cloudera workshop environment
  • Team name for project naming (e.g., Team001-documentanalysis)

Keep This Guide Open

Bookmark this site during the hackathon. Each section includes screenshots so you can follow along step by step.

docs.title: Support
docs.text: If you encounter issues during the lab, reach out to your Cloudera workshop instructor or check the troubleshooting tips in each section.

docs.title: Data Upload and Insertion
docs.text: This section provides sample code and data files for loading campaign metric data into your Cloudera AI project during the hackathon.

docs.title: Artifacts
docs.text:
The following files are available in the zeta-hol repository:

File Description Location sample_metric_data.json Sample campaign metrics (10 records) artifacts/sample_metric_data.json dataload_notebook.ipynb Jupyter notebook for loading and analyzing data artifacts/dataload_notebook.ipynb

docs.title: Getting the Files into Your Project
docs.text: Choose one of these methods:

docs.title: Option 1: Upload via the Data Tab
docs.text:
1. Open your project in Cloudera AI
  2. Click Data in the top navigation
  3. Upload sample_metric_data.json directly

docs.title: Option 2: Clone the Repository
docs.text:
In your workbench terminal:

git clone https://github.com/SuperEllipse/zeta-hol.git
cd zeta-hol

Files will be available at zeta-hol/artifacts/.

docs.title: Option 3: Download Individual Files
docs.text:
curl -O https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SuperEllipse/zeta-hol/main/artifacts/sample_metric_data.json
curl -O https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SuperEllipse/zeta-hol/main/artifacts/dataload_notebook.ipynb

docs.title: Sample Data Schema
docs.text:
The JSON file contains campaign performance metrics:

{
  "id": 1,
  "campaign_id": "CMP-1001",
  "campaign_name": "Summer Email Blast",
  "channel": "email",
  "impressions": 125000,
  "clicks": 3750,
  "conversions": 412,
  "spend_usd": 8500.00,
  "revenue_usd": 24680.50,
  "date": "2026-08-01"
}
Field Type Description id integer Record identifier campaign_id string Unique campaign code campaign_name string Human-readable campaign name channel string Marketing channel (email, push, display, etc.) impressions integer Number of ad impressions clicks integer Number of clicks conversions integer Number of conversions spend_usd float Campaign spend in USD revenue_usd float Revenue attributed in USD date string Date (ISO 8601 format)

docs.title: Using the Notebook
docs.text:
Follow along with the workshop demo recording, which walks through loading sample data step by step.

  1. Upload or clone dataload_notebook.ipynb into your project
  2. Open it in JupyterLab (from your active session)
  3. Run all cells sequentially, as demonstrated in the video

The notebook covers:

  1. Setup — Import libraries
  2. Load JSON — Read sample metric data
  3. Create DataFrame — Convert to pandas
  4. Derived Metrics — Calculate CTR, conversion rate, ROAS, CPC
  5. Aggregation — Summarize by marketing channel
  6. Export — Save to CSV and Parquet
  7. Database Insert — Optional SQLAlchemy example (commented out)

docs.title: Derived Metrics Reference
docs.text: Metric Formula Description CTR clicks / impressions × 100 Click-through rate (%) Conversion Rate conversions / clicks × 100 Conversion rate (%) ROAS revenue / spend Return on ad spend CPC spend / clicks Cost per click

docs.title: Login and Workbench Setup
docs.text: This section covers how to log into the Cloudera Data Platform (CDP) workshop environment and navigate to the shared AI workbench for the Zeta Global hackathon.

docs.title: Step 1: Log In to Cloudera
docs.text:
Open the workshop login URL in your browser:

https://login.cdpworkshops.cloudera.com/auth/realms/field-marketing-amer/protocol/saml/clients/cdp-sso

Enter the credentials provided by your instructor:

Field Value Username or email <provided by your instructor> Password <provided by your instructor>

Click Sign In to authenticate.

Figure 1: Sign in to your account on the FIELD-MARKETING-AMER realm.

Credentials

Your instructor will distribute workshop credentials before the session begins. Do not share credentials outside your team.

docs.title: Step 2: Select Cloudera AI
docs.text:
After logging in, you will land on the CDP home dashboard. Under All Services, locate and click Cloudera AI.

Figure 2: Click the Cloudera AI tile (indicated by the arrow) from the All Services grid.

docs.title: Step 3: Select the Zeta Workbench
docs.text:
On the AI Workbenches tab, find the workbench named zeta1-workbench1. It should show a Ready status with AWS as the cloud provider.

Click the workbench name or the View → button to open it.

Figure 3: Open the zeta1-workbench1 workbench — status should be Ready.

You're In!

Once the workbench opens, you are inside the Cloudera AI environment where all hackathon work takes place. Continue to Project Creation & Runtimes to set up your team project.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Issue Solution Login page does not load Verify the URL and check your network/VPN settings Invalid credentials Confirm username/password with your instructor Workbench not visible Refresh the page; contact your instructor if zeta1-workbench1 is missing Workbench status not Ready Wait a few minutes and refresh; contact support if it persists

docs.title: Project Creation and Runtimes
docs.text: All hackathon work happens inside a Cloudera AI Project. Each team creates one project using the naming convention below and configures the appropriate Python runtime.

docs.title: Step 1: Create a New Project
docs.text:
From the workbench home page, click Create a new project.

Figure 1: Click "Create a new project" to begin.

docs.title: Project Configuration
docs.text:
Fill in the project form as follows:

Field Value Project Owner Your assigned user (e.g., Test001 user001) Project Name TeamName-ProjectName (e.g., Team001-documentanalysis) Project Description Brief description of your hackathon project Project Visibility Private (recommended) Initial Setup Blank

Figure 2: Example project name — team001-project (use your team name + project name).

Naming Convention

Use the format TeamXXX-<descriptive-name> so instructors can easily identify your team's work. Examples:

  • Team001-documentanalysis
  • Team002-customer-segmentation
  • Team003-recommendation-engine

Click Create to provision your project.

docs.title: Step 2: Configure Runtimes
docs.text:
After project creation, configure your session runtime:

Setting Recommended Value Editor JupyterLab Kernel Python 3.12 or higher Edition Standard Python runtime (or Claude Code with CAI Inference for AI-assisted coding — see Claude Private Model) Version Latest available

Python Version

Select Python 3.12 or higher for all notebook and script work. This ensures compatibility with the sample data loading notebook and modern Python libraries.

docs.title: Enabling Additional Runtimes
docs.text:
If you need the Claude Code with CAI Inference runtime:

  1. Open Project Settings
  2. Navigate to Runtimes
  3. Enable Claude Code with CAI Inference
  4. Save settings

You can then select this runtime when starting a new session.

docs.title: What's Next?
docs.text:
Your project is the workspace for all hackathon deliverables. From here:

  • Vibe Coding with Cloudera AI — Set up Cursor or Claude CLI for AI-assisted development
  • Sample Code: Data Upload — Load sample metric data into your project

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Issue Solution Project name already taken Add a suffix or use a more specific project name Runtime not available Enable it in Project Settings → Runtimes Project creation fails Check resource quotas with your instructor

docs.title: Using Claude with a Private Model
docs.text: Cloudera AI provides a pre-configured Claude Code with CAI Inference runtime for the hackathon. This lets you use the Claude CLI directly in your workbench terminal with a private model endpoint — no external API keys required.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
The Claude runtime includes:

  • Claude Code CLI — Interactive AI coding assistant in the terminal
  • Cloudera AI Inference — Private model endpoint (LiteLLM proxy)
  • Pre-configured environment — Ready to use out of the box

docs.title: Step 1: Open Your Project
docs.text: Navigate to the project you created in Project Creation & Runtimes.

docs.title: Step 2: Start a New Session
docs.text:
1. Go to the Sessions tab in your project
  2. Click + New Session

Figure 1: Click "+ New Session" to start a new workbench session.

docs.title: Session Configuration
docs.text:
Configure your session with these settings:

Setting Value Session Name A descriptive name (e.g., claude-dev, team001-session) Editor JupyterLab Kernel Python 3.13 Edition Claude Code with CAI Inference Version Latest (e.g., 2026.08) Enable Spark Off (unless your project requires Spark) Enable GPU Off (unless needed) Resource Group Default CPU Group vCPU / Memory Minimum 2 vCPU / 4 GiB (4 vCPU / 8 GiB recommended)

Figure 2: Select "Claude Code with CAI Inference" edition and appropriate compute profile.

Minimum Resources

Select at least 2 vCPU and 4 GiB memory. The example above uses 4 vCPU / 8 GiB for better performance.

Click Start Session and wait for the session to become ready.

docs.title: Step 3: Open the Terminal
docs.text:
Once your session is running:

  1. In the JupyterLab Launcher, scroll to the Other section
  2. Click Terminal

Figure 3: Click the Terminal icon under "Other" in the Launcher.

docs.title: Step 4: Launch Claude CLI
docs.text:
In the terminal, run:

claude

You will see the Claude Code environment information:

Claude Code + Cloudera AI Inference
Claude Version: claude (2.1.x (Claude Code))
Model: kevinbtalbert/Devstral-Small-2507
Base URL: https://.../openai/v1
Proxy: LiteLLM proxy: http://127.0.0.1:4000

Figure 4: Run claude in the terminal to start the interactive AI assistant.

docs.title: Step 5: Complete the Security Guide
docs.text:
On first launch, Claude presents a security guide. Select these defaults:

Prompt Select Do you trust this folder? 1. Yes, I trust this folder Do you want to use this API Key? No

Press Enter to confirm each selection.

Why These Defaults?

  • Trust folder: Allows Claude to read and modify files in your project directory
  • No API Key: The session uses the pre-configured Cloudera AI Inference proxy — no external key needed

docs.title: Step 6: Start Vibe Coding
docs.text:
You're ready to use Claude for AI-assisted development. Example prompts:

Create a Python script that loads sample_metric_data.json and prints summary statistics

Help me build a data pipeline that reads from the artifacts folder and writes to a DataFrame

Explain the dataload_notebook.ipynb and suggest improvements

docs.title: Useful Claude CLI Commands
docs.text: Command Description claude Start interactive session /help Show available commands /clear Clear conversation history Ctrl+C Exit Claude CLI

docs.title: Environment Details
docs.text:
Your session automatically configures:

Variable Purpose CAI_HOME Cloudera AI Inference configuration directory LiteLLM Proxy Local proxy at http://127.0.0.1:4000 routing to private model Model Pre-selected private model for the workshop

Verify your environment:

echo $CAI_HOME
claude --version

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Issue Solution claude command not found Ensure you selected Claude Code with CAI Inference runtime Session fails to start Increase compute profile to 4 vCPU / 8 GiB Model connection error Restart the session; check LiteLLM proxy is running Security prompt loops Select option 1 (Yes) for folder trust, then No for API key Slow responses Upgrade compute profile or simplify prompts

docs.title: Next Steps
docs.text:
• Load sample data using the Data Upload notebook
  • Connect Cursor via Remote SSH for IDE-based development

docs.title: Using Cursor with Cloudera AI (Remote SSH)
docs.text: This guide explains how to connect Cursor IDE to your Cloudera AI workbench session using Remote SSH and the cdswctl CLI, enabling AI-assisted coding directly against your project environment.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
Before connecting, ensure you have:

  • [x] Completed Login & Workbench Setup
  • [x] Created your team project
  • [x] Cursor IDE installed on your local machine (cursor.com)

docs.title: 1. Generate an SSH Key
docs.text:
ssh-keygen -C cai

Accept the default location, or set the file to /Users/<username>/.ssh/id_cai. Optionally set a passphrase.

docs.title: 2. Copy the Public Key
docs.text:
cat ~/.ssh/id_cai.pub

Copy the entire output line.

docs.title: 3. Add the Key to the Workbench
docs.text: In the Cloudera AI Workbench, go to User Settings → Keys & Access → Remote Editing, paste your public key into SSH Public Key, and click Add.

docs.title: 4. Download the CML CLI Client
docs.text:
On the same Remote Editing page, download the CML CLI client (cdswctl) for your operating system.

On Mac, if the download is blocked: Finder → Control-click → Open.

docs.title: 5. Add cdswctl to Your PATH
docs.text: After downloading, unpack the archive and optionally add cdswctl to your system PATH environment variable.

docs.title: 6. Get Your Legacy API Key
docs.text:
In the Cloudera AI Workbench, go to User Settings → Keys & Access → API Keys and copy the Legacy API Key (not the plain "API Key").

Please feel free to Rotate the key as needed.

docs.title: 7. Create the SSH Config Entry
docs.text:
Add the following entry to ~/.ssh/config:

Host cai-workbench
    HostName localhost
    Port 3735
    User cdsw
    IdentityFile ~/.ssh/id_cai
    StrictHostKeyChecking no
    ServerAliveInterval 60
    ServerAliveCountMax 10

Port Changes Each Session

The Port value will need updating each session — see step 4 under Every-session Steps below.

docs.title: 1. Log In to CAI Workbench Remotely
docs.text:
Use the Legacy API Key, not the API Key ID:

cdswctl login -u https://<workbench-url> -n <username> -y <legacy_api_key>

If Mac prevents you from running the cdswctl command, remove the quarantine attribute:

xattr -d com.apple.quarantine /<PATH>/cdswctl

Wait for "Login succeeded."

docs.title: 2. Start the Endpoint
docs.text:
This creates the session and SSH tunnel. First, list available runtimes:

cdswctl runtimes list

Spin up a session using a specific runtime. For example, -r 116 corresponds to PBJ Workbench / Python 3.10. It takes a minute or two:

cdswctl ssh-endpoint -p <username>/<cai_workbench_project_name> -r 116 -c 2 -m 4

You can verify from the CAI Workbench Project → Sessions tab that the new session has been created.

docs.title: 3. Read the Port
docs.text:
The command prints connection details:

You can SSH to the session using
    ssh -p <PORT> cdsw@localhost

Leave this terminal open — this process is the tunnel.

docs.title: 4. Update the Port in SSH Config
docs.text: If <PORT> differs from what is saved in ~/.ssh/config (it changes every session), edit the Port line under cai-workbench to match.

docs.title: 5. Sanity Check (Optional)
docs.text:
In a second terminal:

ssh -p <PORT> cdsw@localhost

Run whoami — it should return <username>. Type exit to leave.

docs.title: 6. Connect in Cursor
docs.text:
1. Press Cmd+Shift+P (Mac) or Ctrl+Shift+P (Windows/Linux)
  2. Select Connect via SSH: Connect to Host
  3. Choose cai-workbench
  4. Enter your key passphrase if prompted
  5. File → Open Folder → /home/cdsw

Your SSH connection to the CAI session is ready for use in Cursor.

docs.title: 7. Shut Down When Done
docs.text: Press Ctrl+C in the cdswctl terminal to shut down the session and stop consuming workbench resources.

docs.title: Alternative: Claude CLI
docs.text: If you prefer working entirely in the browser without Remote SSH, see Claude with Private Model for using the Claude CLI directly in the workbench terminal.
